attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. No one else is being quoted.

semantics.note: He wrote a flat 'will' with a dated horizon, so this is a scorable forecast. The H200 clause is split off correctly. The 'almost no route' qualifier and the timing tied to the expected order are both kept.

contract.note: The plain reading (meaningful legal routes to protection largely gone by Dec 14) is ordinary and fair. It treats the order's issuance as an antecedent, which slightly conflicts with the revision, but the order did issue, so the result is the same either way. It also fails under a narrower AI-specific reading, because state AI laws stayed in force.

evidence.note: Signed order dated Dec 11, 2025. Its operative steps (task force, Commerce report, policy statements, legislative recommendation) all happen later, and it says it will be implemented consistent with applicable law. Nothing in it removes protections on signature.
Law-firm analysis of the order, published before the evaluation date. It says the order does not purport to preempt state law and advises businesses to keep complying with state AI laws.
NY AG release of Dec 10 showing existing state criminal and licensing law applied to harmful chatbot conduct. It sets the baseline the day before the order.
California advisory from January 2025 listing existing laws that apply to AI. It covers an earlier period, so it is background only.
IAPP report of Dec 12 on funding pressure and future agency mandates. It shows the intent to curb state laws through later steps, not protections already removed by the deadline.

reviews.rationale: The order issued Dec 11, 2025 and the Dec 14 deadline has passed. The order's own text and the legal analysis show it relied on later litigation, agency action and funding levers, not immediate preemption. Existing state and general protective laws still applied at the deadline. This meets the contradiction condition, not the support condition.
